# Motion model comparison — milestone 1

*Generated by `compare.py` on 2026-10-25 and copied here so the result is visible in git; `out/` itself is not tracked. Re-running `compare.py` rewrites `out/<listing>/scorecard.md`, not this file.*

Listing `demo-001` · 10 photos · target 30s · plan totals 30.00s.

Every backend was given the identical shot plan: same photos, same order, same camera move per photo, same per-shot length, same prompt. `kenburns` is the control — ffmpeg pan-and-zoom on the real photograph, no generated pixels, no cost. A model has to be visibly better than it to be worth paying for.

## Cost

| Backend | $/s | Clip lengths | Billed for a 30s walkthrough | Cost | vs control |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| ffmpeg Ken Burns (control) | 0.0000 | any | 30s | $0.00 | — |
| Seedance 2.0 Fast | 0.2419 | 3–12s | 35s (5s of it thrown away) | $8.47 | +$8.47 |
| Kling 3.0 Pro | 0.1120 | 5s or 10s | 50s (20s of it thrown away) | $5.60 | +$5.60 |
| Runway Gen-4 Turbo | 0.0500 | 5s or 10s | 50s (20s of it thrown away) | $2.50 | +$2.50 |

The fixed clip length is the thing to notice. A 30-second walkthrough from 10 photos wants shots of about three seconds. Models that only generate 5s or 10s clips bill 50s for those 30s — two thirds of the spend is footage the edit trims off. Either pay it, or cut the walkthrough to six 5-second shots instead of ten 3-second ones.

## Quality

| Backend | Opening SSIM vs photo | Drift first→last | Worst jump | Flagged | Status |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| ffmpeg Ken Burns (control) | 0.917 | 0.904 | 2.1x | 0 | measured |
| Seedance 2.0 Fast | — | — | — | — | simulated — no key |
| Kling 3.0 Pro | — | — | — | — | simulated — no key |
| Runway Gen-4 Turbo | — | — | — | — | simulated — no key |

What the numbers mean, and their limits, is in `qc.py`. In short: **opening SSIM** is how closely the first generated frame still matches the photograph that was handed in — the clearest sign of a model repainting a room rather than filming it. **Drift** falls as the camera moves, so it is only readable against the control on the same shot. **Jump** is the worst single-frame change relative to the typical one; a gimbal move is flat, a morph spikes.

The control does not score 1.000 on opening SSIM because a push-in starts already slightly inside the frame. That is the floor the models are measured against, not a defect.

## Where this stands

1 of 4 backends produced a finished 30s clip here. 3 were costed but not run, for want of an API key (FAL_KEY, RUNWAYML_API_SECRET).
